findings.evidence: KEY ASSERTION for Wave G is 'lockout throttle fires'. The spec (test-e2e-abuse-G-auth.spec.js:131-167) posts a FIXED email ADMIN_EMAIL='admin@lecayenne.fr' + a constant wrong password 14 times in ~8s (network.json ts 1780457489277 -> 1780457497402, all same key). The login route HAS throttle:login-lockout (routes/api.php:161); the limiter is Limit::perMinutes(10, 10) keyed by 'email|ip' (RouteServiceProvider.php:247-265, max_attempts=10 / decay=10min). With a FIXED email+ip, attempt 11 MUST return 429. OBSERVED: 03-login-throttle.network.json = 14 consecutive POST /api/auth/login -> 400, ZERO 429. The brute-force account-lockout did NOT fire. The spec only soft-warns (console.warn) and still PASSES, so the 5/5 green hid an unenforced security control. The throttle loop (spec lines 162-167) contains no rate-limit-bucket clear, so the cause is product/runtime (limiter key, cache driver coherence, or bad-creds 400 short-circuiting before the limiter decrements), not a test artifact.
findings.fix_hint: GO-LIVE CHECKLIST: ensure prod .env sets LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=10 (or unset -> default 10). BACKLOG (UNI-03 style): fold a LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS<=N ceiling into the AppServiceProvider production boot guard so a misconfigured prod .env hard-fails at boot like POS_SIMULATION_HARDWARE.
findings.resolution: DOWNGRADED P1->P2 after root-cause. NOT a code defect: limiter is correctly wired (RouteServiceProvider:247-265, Limit::perMinutes(decay,max)->by(email|ip)->429) and PROVEN to fire in prod config. The cause is dev .env:80 LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS=500 (an intentional E2E-convenience override documented in .env.example:34,46). Prod-safe: config/auth.php default=10 AND .env.example template=10. RISK: the AppServiceProvider boot guard does NOT assert LOGIN_LOCKOUT_MAX_ATTEMPTS, so a prod .env carrying a high value would ship brute-force protection neutered with nothing catching it.

findings.evidence: 04b-login-reload-authcheck.console.json + .network.json show POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/api/auth/authcheck -> 405 (Method Not Allowed) with a doubled /api/api/ prefix. ROOT CAUSE IS THE SPEC, NOT THE PRODUCT: spec line 212 calls window.axios.post('/api/auth/authcheck') but window.axios already carries baseURL='/api', producing /api/api/auth/authcheck. The real application code is correct: resources/js/store/modules/auth.js:67 calls axios.post('auth/authcheck') -> /api/auth/authcheck, and the SAME quartet shows that correct call returning 200 (04b-login-reload-authcheck.network.json first entry, ts 1780457504470). Token-persistence-across-reload is genuinely proven (post-reload /admin URL guard + the 200 authcheck). The 405 console error is a test-harness artifact, not application code, so it does not count as a category-9 console error against the product.
findings.fix_hint: Spec hygiene only: in test-e2e-abuse-G-auth.spec.js:212 change window.axios.post('/api/auth/authcheck') to window.axios.post('auth/authcheck') (or use a leading-slash-free path) so the probe stops doubling the baseURL. No product change.

findings.evidence: AUDIT_PLAN Wave G state 06 is meant to be the 'reset form (validation)'. The captured PNG is NOT a reset form -- it is the standard login page ('Bon Retour' / Email / Mot De Passe / Connexion). The reset-password route self-redirected to login because no OTP/resetToken store state is set (documented in spec header lines 63-64: ResetPasswordComponent.mounted -> emailChecking() redirects to auth.verifyEmail unless store.resetInfo.{email,resetToken} are set; OTP delivery is SMS/email-gated and not wired in dev). The gate behavior (no token -> bounce to login) is acceptable, but it means the reset-password FORM itself and its validation were never visually or technically audited in this wave. Disclose as a coverage gap so it is on record.
findings.fix_hint: To actually exercise the reset form, seed store.resetInfo.{email,resetToken} (or stub the OTP step) before navigating to the reset route, or add a dev-only ENV path that wires a fake OTP. Track as a follow-up capture; not a product defect.
